title: A change-review request that never names a skill loads change-reviewer, and the answer reaches the new function
prompt: 这是本次提交的改动：changes.diff 是差异，page.py 是改动后的文件。帮我审查有没有会改变行为的问题，指出函数名和触发条件。不要改代码。

fixture.notes: The diff adds total_pages() as len(items) // size, so a 10-item list with size 3 renders 3 pages and loses the fourth. page.py is the post-change file; nothing in the fixture states the defect.

graders.expects: every read_skill call used name=change-reviewer; no other workflow was loaded instead
the answer names total_pages, the function the diff introduces, so it read the diff rather than the prompt

cleanup: Discard the trial workspace; the fixture directory is never written to.
notes: This case grades the weakest claim of the five: naming total_pages proves the diff was opened, not that the off-by-one was found. No deterministic check can decide 'the review found the defect' without judging prose, and an uncalibrated rubric may not gate a trial, so the finding itself stays unasserted and is reported as such. The skill read is the measurement; this grader only keeps a pass from being a guess.
